title: Juneteenth, Fourth of July and Mexican holidays in Texas
summary: Texas holidays: Juneteenth barbecues, fireworks, Sixteenth of September and Cinco de Mayo dances.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Well, they have a holiday down there. There used to be a holiday down there to Negroes. We used to celebrate it, which was the 19th of June. That's, in other words, it's a Freedom Day. Juneteenth. I heard of it. Juneteenth. I heard of it. They're fastly getting away from that. The young ones don't want to associate themselves with-
They don't want to celebrate Freedom. No. That's funny with all that talk about Freedom.
But they don't want that as an example to where the full patterns come from.
But what goes on on Juneteenth?

Not anything anymore, but in the old days, they used to gather and they'd have barbecue, soda water, beer, and a band. And it would last all day, starting tomorrow and then last on until 12.1.2. Probably 90.
What about the 4th of July? What would you do?
Well, the 4th of July, everybody celebrates it. And, of course, you have your Mexican population on there that celebrates the day, Seseis, September.
The what?

The day, Seseis, September, which means the 16th of September. That's their Freedom Day. Freedom from Mexico. And, of course, the other holidays are in there, the national holidays, Columbus Day and Thanksgiving.
Would you have a barbecue on the 4th of July?
Yeah, they have outdoor barbecues. Friends gather and families gather on their lawns and things like that and barbecue.
What about fireworks in Texas? When would you shoot the fireworks?
They'll still shoot them.
4th of July? Sure. Christmas?
They shoot them any time they feel like it. It's against the law, but they find a way to shoot them any hour.
Well, in New Orleans, it seems to me people shoot fireworks at Christmas and I'm trying to remember them.
Just a couple of days. Well, they'll shoot fireworks in Texas whenever they feel like shooting.

Yeah, it might be July the 1st or January the 1st. That's right. Just so you felt like shooting fireworks and shoot them off. I just wondered. It seems to me that different sections, they have different customs. I mean, 4th of July, certainly everywhere. Everywhere. But other days.

Well, those are the big things in there. And of course, the Mexican population also has another one, Cinco de Mayo. That's the 5th of May. Did you play for them? Oh, I played for a number of Mexican dances.
Yeah, but I mean for those days.
Yeah, sometimes we were.
How do they celebrate it? I mean, they must have, you say dancing? Food?
Yeah, the regular routine of any other thing you see around here. Band playing, dancing, singing, food and drinks. Of course, they had their fabulous costumes, if they were.
Oh, yeah.
The traditional Mexican costumes.
